newsitem.title: RUSSIA: China leader to receive warm welcome in Russia.
newsitem.headline: China leader to receive warm welcome in Russia.

text.p: Russia was preparing a red carpet welcome for Chinese President Jiang Zemin on Tuesday at the start of a five-day official visit intended to build ties between the two vast countries.

"Rapprochement with China has become a dominant theme in Russian foreign policy," the newspaper Kommersant Daily said. "Moscow and Beijing are chanting the formula of their 'partnership aimed at strategic cooperation in the 21st century' as if it were a mantra."

President Boris Yeltsin was interrupting a holiday in the Black Sea resort of Sochi to give Jiang a formal welcome on Wednesday. Jiang, due to arrive at 1000 GMT on Tuesday, was to be met at the airport by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
During the visit, Yeltsin and Jiang will sign a political declaration outlining a joint vision of the future world order.

The two leaders will be joined by the presidents of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan to sign a treaty on reducing armed forces along the former Soviet-Chinese border. Details of the treaty have not been made public.
Moscow, wary of NATO's plans to expand eastwards, has made Jiang's visit a hugely symbolic event.

Jiang, who has a good knowledge of the Russian language and literature, will go on Friday to Yasnaya Polyana, the estate of writer and philosopher Leo Tolstoy about 200 km (130 miles) south of Moscow.
Moscow and Beijing have made clear they are poised to set an example for other countries on how to maintain security and build bilateral ties.

"This new type of relationship includes a refusal to take part in military blocs, ruling out confrontation and any menace to third parties," Interfax news agency quoted the Chinese ambassador to Moscow, Li Fenglin, as saying.

Yeltsin's spokesman, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, underlined the importance of the joint political declaration -- the first such document signed since Moscow and Beijing started repairing ties in the late 1980s after more than two decades of hostility.

"In this declaration...Russia and China will express their vision of how to form the new international order in the 21st century and will speak out against claims by any country to the role of absolute leader," he told Interfax.
He named no state but Moscow and Beijing have been critical of Washington's domination of the post-Cold War world order.

"The spirit of (Jiang's) visit is in sharp contrast to the tendencies emerging in the west such as NATO plans to expand," Itar-Tass news agency quoted Igor Rogachev, the Russian ambassador to China, as saying on Monday.

Moscow also hopes for better trade relations with Beijing that would bring greater access to the vast Chinese market and to markets in South-East Asia and the Pacific Rim. But it must solve some problems if the honeymoon with Beijing is to go on.
Itar-Tass news agency said two-way trade reached $6.9 billion in 1996, 25 percent more than in 1995. But the balance is lop-sided in Russia's favour to the tune of about $3.5 billion.
Russian officials have said that trade turnover could reach $8-10 billion in 1997 and $20 billion by the end of the century.
Russia hopes to boost arms sales to China from around $1 billion a year. Some estimates say this could be up to 30 percent of Moscow's overall arms exports.

The two countries, however, have yet to complete demarcation of their long border. Leaders of Far Eastern regions of Russia say a proposed new borderline is unjust but the government has dismissed their complaints.
